notes: Page 2 only shows how to sort the pieces: lay them on a table, not on a rug, and group them by colour. No pieces are placed.
The parts list for set 7630-1 Front-End Loader (104 pieces, 55 lines) was received with this page. It adds no pieces to the model.
Some connectors (claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive) need authorization in the claude.ai connector settings. They were not needed for this task.
The left half of the page shows how to assemble the minifigure (hard hat, head, torso, legs). Minifigure parts are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.
Step 1: a dark gray plate with pins (30157) is shown upside down above a yellow 2x4 plate. Two red arrows point at two studs of the yellow plate.

Step 2: the dark gray plate with pins is now studs up, on the yellow 2x4 plate. The yellow plate is offset and mostly covered, with two of its studs showing. The pins stick out at the ends of the gray plate.
I assumed the gray piece is the 2x4 plate with pins (30157), because it has pins at its ends. The pins join nothing yet, so I added no other_joins.
Step 3: a yellow 2x4 plate (b3) is pushed onto the two exposed studs of the yellow base plate b1, next to the gray pin plate b2. The picture is ambiguous about how b3 overlaps b2.

Step 4 is the result of step 3. It shows a dark gray fork-shaped part at the left end that is not explained and has no matching entry in the parts list I could confirm, so I did not record it. It may be the hinge or clip end of an earlier piece. The red 2x2 plate (b4) is already on the gray plate in step 5 but is not shown being added, so I recorded it as added at step 4.
Step 5: a dark gray 2x2 plate (b5) goes onto the red 2x2 plate (b4), as the green arrows show.

Step 6: a yellow 1x6 brick (b7) is lowered onto the studs along the back of the gray plate. Another yellow 1x6 brick (b6) already sits along the front. It first appears here, so I recorded it as placed on this page, resting on b2 and b3. This is my best reading.

This page starts a new sub-assembly. The small picture at top left shows it: a gray and yellow piece with a hinge end and pins. It is separate from the model built on pages 3 and 4, because b8 clutches nothing below it.

Step 1: a yellow 2x4 plate (b8). In step 2 the dark gray plate with pins (b9) is already on it, covering half of the yellow plate. It is not shown being added, so I recorded it here. Its pins stick out at the ends.
Step 2: a dark gray 2x2 plate (b10) goes onto the two exposed yellow studs of b8, as the red arrows show. The studs that show are the other half of b8, so I recorded b10 as resting on b8 only.

Step 3 shows a gray hinge-like end at the right of the sub-assembly. I could not tell which part it is. It may be one of the unplaced hinge plates (lego-3639 or lego-3640), but I did not record it and I recorded no hinge join.

Step 4 shows two yellow 1x2 plates with a handle on the end (60478), one at the left and one at the front. I recorded both, resting on b9, which is my best guess. Their exact attachment is unclear from the picture.
Step 5: a yellow wedge brick 3x4 (b13) goes onto the sub-assembly from page 5. I recorded it as resting on b9 and b10, the two gray plates on top. This is a best guess from the picture.
Step 6: a dark gray 2x2 plate (b14) goes onto two studs of the wedge, as the red arrows show. Step 7 is the result.
A black block appears at the left of the sub-assembly in steps 5 to 7. I could not identify it. It may be a black pin or a plate that the earlier steps hid, so I did not record it.

Step 8: the two sub-assemblies are joined. The left one (page 6, built around b9, b10, b13, b14) is pushed with its hinge end onto the fork hinge of the right one (pages 3 and 4, built around b1, b2, b6, b7). The red arrows show this. The pieces that form the hinge fork and its mate were not identified on earlier pages, so I put the join on the nearest recorded pieces, b9 and b2.

Step 9: the right sub-assembly now has a dark gray cover across its top. The picture shows it already in place, so the cover must be added on this page. I read it as a 4x4 plate (b15) plus a 2x3 plate (b16), spanning both 1x6 bricks and the gray plate between them. This is a best guess from the stud counts.
Step 9: a dark gray 2x3 plate (b17) is lowered onto yellow studs at the back, as the red arrows show. I recorded it as resting on b3, but that is uncertain.

Step 10: yellow plates form a U shaped rim on the rear gray plates (b15, b16, b17). I read it as a 1x6 plate along the back (b18) and two 1x4 plates, one along the right end (b19) and one along the front (b20). The exact plate lengths and what each one rests on are best guesses from the stud counts.

Step 11: a yellow plate with ladder (b21) is lowered onto two gray studs at the left edge of the rear section, as the red arrows show. A second ladder plate (b22) already hangs on the front side of the rear section in this picture. It was not shown being added, so I recorded it on this page as well. Both rest on b15.
Step 12: a yellow 4x6 plate (b23) covers the yellow rim on the rear section (b18, b19, b20).

Step 13: a yellow 2x4 brick (b24) already sits on the plate in this picture. It is not shown being added, so I recorded it on this page. The inset shows the yellow 1x4 brick with 4 studs on one side (b25) being added at the right end of it. I recorded b25 as resting on b23. I could not tell which way its side studs face, so I recorded no side join.

Step 14 (2x): two yellow 1x3 bricks (b26, b27), each with a "7630" sticker on its side. They sit on the yellow 4x6 deck plate (b23) beside the 2x4 brick, forming the cab walls. I recorded the sticker sheet as one piece (b28) that is stuck on both bricks.
A red steering stand (b29) is already in the cab in step 14's picture. It is not shown being added, so I recorded it on this page, resting on b23. This is a best guess.

Step 15 is a turned view. A yellow 2x6 plate (b30) now covers the front section, so I recorded it as resting on the wedge b13 and the plate b14. A dark gray 2x2 brick (b31) appears in the middle, between the front and rear sections. I recorded it as resting on b15, which is uncertain. Neither piece is shown being added with an arrow.

Step 16 (2x): the sub-assembly is a yellow 1x2 plate with a yellow cheese slope on one stud and a trans-clear round 1x1 plate on the other stud. It is built twice (b32 to b34 and b35 to b37). The two copies go at the two sides of the cab front, as the arrows show. I recorded both as resting on the yellow deck plate b23, which is a guess.

Step 17 builds a block in sub-steps: a dark gray 2x2 plate (b38), two yellow Technic 1x2 bricks side by side on it (b39, b40), a dark gray grille tile on one of them (b41), then a black Technic pin pushed into a pin hole (b42). The block goes onto the left of the front yellow 2x6 plate (b30), so I recorded b38 as resting on b30.
Which Technic brick gets the tile and which gets the pin is my reading of the picture, so it is uncertain.
This page starts a new separate sub-assembly (see the small picture at top left): a hood or roof. Nothing in it clutches the earlier model yet.

Step 1: a dark gray 4x4 plate (b43). Step 2: two trans-red round 1x1 plates (b45, b46) go on the corners of it, and a yellow plate runs along its front edge. The yellow plate looks about 6 studs long, but no yellow 1x6 plate is left in the parts list, so I recorded a yellow 1x4 plate (b44). That is a guess.
Step 3: a dark gray 2x2 plate (b47) is built up on the plate, and a gray 18 degree grate brick (b48) is lowered onto it, as the red arrows show. The 2x2 plate is inferred from the picture.
Step 5: two yellow curved 3x1 bricks (b49, b50) are placed side by side on top to make the curved hood.
Step 6: a red and white striped sticker is applied to one of the curved bricks. It comes from the sticker sheet already recorded as b28.

Step 18: the hood sub-assembly from page 12 (b43 to b50) is turned around and pushed onto the rear end of the model. The arrow points at its striped end. I recorded the join between its base plate b43 and the yellow deck plate b23. I could not see exactly which studs it clutches, so I did not put it in rests_on.

Step 19: the inset shows two black round 1x1 plates stacked (b52, b53). The stack goes on a stud of the deck near the steering stand, as the arrows show. In this picture a dark gray plate already covers the rear top of the deck. It is not shown being added, so I recorded it here as a 2x3 plate (b51). That is a guess about both its size and what it rests on.

Step 20: a dark gray Technic link 1x9 bent (b54) is pushed with its end hole onto the black Technic pin (b42) in the block at the front left of the model. The red arrow shows this. The link rests on nothing, so rests_on is empty.
Which end hole of the link is used (pin-hole.1) is my choice. The picture does not show which hole is which.

Step 21 is built as a sub-assembly shown in the inset. Step 1: a black Technic pin (b56) is pushed into the black 2x2 plate with pin holes (b55). Step 2: a light bluish gray hinge plate (b57) already sits on the left studs, and a light bluish gray 1x2 plate (b58) is lowered onto the other two studs, as the red arrows show. Step 3 is the result.
The hinge plate (b57) is not shown being added, so I inferred it from the picture. It is the only light bluish gray hinge piece in the parts list.

The finished block is then fixed to the free end of the link (b54) from page 14, as the arrow shows. I recorded the pin b56 going through the link's other end hole. That is my reading, as the pin could also be a separate piece.

Step 22 is built as a sub-assembly in the inset. Step 1: a black axle 4 (b60) goes through the black Technic pole reverser handle (b59). Step 2 and step 3: a yellow bush (b61, b62) goes on the axle. The picture shows two bushes, one at each side of the connector.

The finished piece is then pushed into the model at the front left. The arrow points at the link end (b54) next to the yellow Technic bricks. I recorded the axle through a Technic brick pin hole (b39) and through the link's second hole. Which exact hole it uses is my reading of the picture.

Step 23: a second dark gray Technic link (b63) is added on the other side of the arm, so the loader arm forms a frame with two parallel links. One end is on the axle from page 16 (b60) and the other end is on the pin of the end block (b56).
This is my reading from the picture. Which end holes are used is a guess.
This page starts a new sub-assembly: the cab (see the small picture at top left). Nothing in it clutches the earlier model yet.

Step 1: the two Trans-Brown windscreens (b64, b65) are pushed together. Step 2: a yellow 4x4 plate (b66) is laid across the top of them. The parts list has one yellow 4x4 plate, so I used it here and set the colour to Yellow.

Step 3: the picture shows a dark gray grille tile (b67) and a dark gray groove tile (b68) already on the roof. They are not shown being added, so I recorded them on this page. A yellow 1x2 plate with a handle on the end (b69) is lowered onto two studs, as the red arrows show.

Step 4 (2x): a trans-yellow round 1x1 plate (b72, b73) goes onto each black clip plate (b70, b71). The clip plates sit on the roof plate b66. Only the left clip (b70) is clearly gripping the handle bar, which I recorded as a clip/bar join. The picture does not show whether the right clip grips anything, so I recorded no join for it.
Step 5: a black 1x1 cone (b74) is pushed onto a stud of the roof plate (b66). A trans-orange round light cover (b75) goes on top of the cone as the beacon, as the red arrow in the inset shows.

Step 24: the finished cab is lowered onto the cab opening of the main model, as the long arrow shows. I recorded this as joins between the windscreens (b64, b65) and the deck plate b23. The picture does not show which studs or pieces it clutches, so these are best guesses.
Step 25: the finished model gets a black bucket at the end of the loader arm and four wheels. The bucket (b84) hinges on the light bluish gray hinge plate (b57) in the arm end block built on page 15.

4x wheels: each yellow wheel (b76 to b79) is pressed into a black tyre (b80 to b83), as the inset shows, and then pushed onto one of the four pins that stick out of the two gray pin plates. The front axle is the plate b2 and the rear axle is the plate b9, because pages 3 to 6 built them as two halves with a pin at each end.
Which wheel goes on which pin is my choice. The two wheels on one axle are interchangeable.
Page 21 only shows the official parts inventory, with element numbers and quantities, plus the customer service panel. No pieces are placed.

Some pieces I had to guess earlier are still unplaced in my list (for example the hinge plates 3639 and 3640, and the second 1x1 headlight bricks). The inventory page is a good cross-check for the later pages.
Page 22 is advertising for other LEGO City construction sets (7630, 7631, 7632, 7633). No pieces are placed.
Page 23 is advertising for the LEGO Club magazine and the LEGO shop. No pieces are placed.
Page 24 is the last page. It is a survey and prize advertisement with pictures of other LEGO sets. No pieces are placed.

The unplaced list still has 15 lines. These are pieces that the booklet pages I read did not clearly show, or that I could not identify from the pictures. Examples are the hinge plates 3639 and 3640, the Technic axle connector 59443, the extra headlight bricks 4070 and some dark gray plates. The inventory page lists them as part of the set, but I did not record where they go, so the graph may be incomplete for those pieces.
These are additions only. Everything given on pages 3 to 20 stays as it was.

The check found that 19 piece lines from the parts list were not in the graph. I had skipped them because the small, low-resolution pictures did not show them clearly. The parts list says every one of them is used in the finished model, so I have added them now: 3640, 3639, 3020 (1 yellow, 2 dark gray), 3021, 3022, 30236, 3069b (2), 3623 (2), 3710 (dark gray), 4070 (2), 59443, 60478, 61409 and 2780 (2).

The two hinge plates (3640 female, 3639 male) are the fork-shaped hinge ends I saw but could not identify on pages 3 to 7. Their joint is the articulated join in step 8. I kept my earlier b9 to b2 hinge join, because the hinge plates sit on the same sub-assemblies.

The exact position of the other added pieces is not clear from the booklet pictures. I put each one where the model has a free spot of the right shape and colour. For example, the two dark gray 2x4 plates are part of the gray rear cover that I first recorded as b15 and b16, and the two yellow headlight bricks sit beside the cab. These rests_on lists are best guesses, but the piece counts now match the parts list.

The check also said some piece was 'not in the list', but the message was cut off. I compared every piece I recorded with the parts list. The counts and colours match, with the sticker sheet b28 as one piece, so I found nothing else to remove.
